Solipsistic

/sol-ip-SIS-tik/ - the stress falls on SIS · adjective

What It Means

Solipsistic means treating one's own mind or self as the only thing that truly exists or matters.

The band's documentary is oddly solipsistic — three of the four members appear only as elbows at the edge of the drummer's close-ups.

Worked Example

The captain's log from the disastrous voyage is notoriously solipsistic: the reef, the storm, and the mutinous crew each appear only as obstacles standing between the captain and his breakfast.

Solipsistic is more precise than 'selfish' because selfishness is about hoarding advantages; solipsism is about attention — behaving as if no mind but yours is quite real. The solipsistic writer isn't cruel to other people; other people simply never come into focus.

How Solipsistic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

self-centered

self-centered: puts its own needs first; solipsistic barely registers that others exist to have needs

narcissistic

narcissistic: in love with its own image and hungry for admirers; solipsism forgets the audience entirely

Antonyms

empathetic

empathetic: tuned to what someone else is feeling — a word from this unit's own list

outward-looking

outward-looking: attention aimed at the world beyond the self

How Strong Is It? — self-absorbed → egocentric → solipsistic

self-absorbed vs. solipsistic

self-absorbed vs. solipsistic: Self-absorbed people sink into their own concerns but can be pulled back out — the mildest rung, well below solipsistic.

egocentric vs. solipsistic

egocentric vs. solipsistic: Egocentric goes further than self-absorbed — every event measured by its effect on me — yet it still stops short of solipsistic, which quietly doubts the rest of you are fully there at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of solipsistic.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — sol-

Root — sol-: alone (Latin solus)

Root — ips-

Root — ips-: self (Latin ipse)

Suffix — -ist

Suffix — -ist: one who believes in

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of

Put it together

Put it together: Sol- (Latin solus, 'alone') + ips- (ipse, 'self') + -ist + -ic = characteristic of the alone-self believer. Philosophers coined solipsism for the position that only one's own mind is certain to exist; everyday English borrowed it for people who merely live as if that were true.

Use the root in a new word: solo

Use the root in a new word: solo: After the duo split, she recorded a solo album with no other musician on any track.

Root Check

Word Choice

intellectual / critical

Solipsistic is the heavyweight complaint about self-focus — reviews and essays use it when a work treats the world as scenery for one mind. For garden-variety self-focus, 'self-centered' is honest and shorter. Its unit-mate sophomoric mocks a different flaw: the sophomoric performer shows off badly for an audience; the solipsistic one has forgotten the audience exists.
